subject: Post-call: NewRipple pilot fit & SDK/streaming action plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@newripple.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: NewRipple pilot fit & SDK/streaming action plan

Samir / Angela — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can move to a technical pilot that demonstrates the integration patterns we discussed. I captured the pain, goals, and the concrete asks below.

What we heard (pain + goals)
- Search/retrieval reranking is inconsistent at scale: current pipeline has high tail latency and cost when the candidate set grows.
- Need structured outputs from the model (JSON with strict schema) for downstream automation.
- Real-time interactive flows require streaming function-calls (partial results + function invocation) to avoid long blocking calls in the UI.
- Embedding drift across batches — you want deterministic behavior + reproducible vectors for nightly reindexing.

Redwood fit & technical approach (summary)
- Streaming + function-calls: we can expose an SDK path supporting streaming tokens + on-the-fly function invocation. This preserves interactivity while keeping 95th percentile latency under target for small to medium sessions.
- Structured outputs: we recommend using our schema-anchored function-calling path with a small validation shim in your service to catch schema drift.
- Embeddings / rerank: batching, prefix/KV caching, and a quantization profile for your embedding model should reduce per-query cost. We'll propose an embedding batching window tuned to your traffic.
- SDK changes we propose (minimal, backwards-compatible):
  1) new streaming client method: Client.streamGenerate(params, onToken) — supports partial func_call signals
  2) optional schema validation helper: Client.validateSchema(schema, output) — returns structured errors for your sidecar
  3) batchEmbed(inputs, options) with guaranteed order-preserving ids for reindexing

Attachments: NR-Design-Notes.pdf (high-level sketch + sample API), NR-SLO-Proposal.xlsx (latency/cost targets and measurement plan).

Concrete next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Technical deep-dive (30–60m) w/ eng team — proposed week of Sep 12 — owners: Ben (infra/latency), Jordan (SDK).
2) You send a 1k-sample prompt set + representative traffic profile (p95 tokens/session, concurrent sessions) — owner: NewRipple — ETA Sep 10.
3) Redwood to produce a pilot microbenchmark plan including expected 95p latency and cost delta for streaming vs batch — owner: Ben — draft by Sep 14.
4) If pilot looks good, sign a 3-month proof-of-value pilot (Dedicated or Hosted with reserved capacity) — commercial follow-up from our CS team.

Open questions (please confirm)
- Do you need a hard SLA for the pilot or is measurement sufficient to evaluate?
- Will the pilot handle PII data? If yes, we need to scope a Private deployment or dedicated tenancy for the proof.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the deep-dive once I get availability from your engineering team.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0164

(On attachments: I’ve included a short design sketch and a proposed SLO spreadsheet as placeholders; we can iterate after the deep-dive.)
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@newripple.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Angela Ortiz <angela.ortiz@newripple.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: NewRipple pilot fit & SDK/streaming action plan

Thanks Mina — that’s very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and items from our side: 

1) Traffic profile
- Typical traffic: ~1200 total requests/minute at peak, median session tokens ~230, p95 tokens/session ~1,200. Concurrent interactive sessions we expect ~60 during peak.

2) Dataset / PII
- The initial sample will be scrubbed. We do have a subset that contains limited customer identifiers; we’ll flag it. For the pilot we prefer Hosted with dedicated capacity if possible but we may require a Private option after seeing the results.

3) Latency expectations
- For interactive flows we’d like end-to-end p95 < 450ms for streaming token delivery (partial tokens are okay), and overall function-call completion < 900ms for common 1–2 turn flows. Can your microbenchmark target that range with 4 GPUs?

4) Commercial / timeline
- We’re ready to start a pilot as soon as the technical plan is agreed. Pricing/credits will be needed to cover a 3-week microbenchmark. Can you share a rough estimate (ballpark) ahead of the deep-dive so procurement can budget?

I’ll attach the sample prompts today (few hundred rows) and will follow up about scheduling the deep-dive — prefer Sep 13 or 14 US morning.

—
Samir Patel
Head of Product, NewRipple
samir.patel@newripple.ai

Mina — copying internal notes/plan.

Plan for microbenchmark (owner / runbook)
- Bench target: simulate 1,200 req/min, 60 concurrent sessions, p95 tokens/session 1,200.
- Setup: use two worker services to emulate streaming behavior + function-call hooks.
- Hardware: start with 4 x A10-equivalent, measure p50/p95/p99 for streaming token latency and func_call completion.
- Metrics: per-token latency distribution, GPU utilization, network egress, cost per 1,000 tokens.

Immediate actions
- Jordan: prepare small SDK branch with streamGenerate and validateSchema stubs + sample JS client by Sep 11.
- Ben: draft benchmark plan and cluster spec by Sep 14.
- Mina: confirm deep-dive slot Sep 13 09:00 PT (tentative) and collect the prompt sample from Samir.

We’ll include a short runbook that NewRipple can run against their sample dataset if they want to reproduce results themselves.

—
Ben Carter
